note.headline: Small dip; SPY and QQQ hold long trends but stay below 50-day averages

summary.thesis: Both indices sit between their trend lines. They are above their 200-day averages, so the long trend holds. They are below their 50-day averages, so the short trend is broken. Fear reads normal, but only 25% of stocks are above their 50-day averages.
summary.decision: Selective for long-term buyers. Stand aside for swing setups until QQQ closes above its 50-day average.
summary.act_at: QQQ close above 718.46 (50-day average) or SPY close above 764.43 (50-day average) to lean in more. SPY close below 728.99 or QQQ close below 680.94 (200-day averages) to stand aside.

note.happening: As of Nov 12, SPY closed at 757.12, down -0.35% on the day. QQQ closed at 688.17, down -0.32%. This was a quiet giveback after the prior session's bounce. Over 5 days both are up: SPY 3.29% and QQQ 6.35%. Over 20 days both are still down: SPY -1.9% and QQQ -5.47%. Both indices set their 1-month low closes on Nov 5, at 733.00 for SPY and 647.05 for QQQ, and have rebounded since. They remain short of their 1-month highs: 773.09 for SPY on Oct 21 and 728.00 for QQQ on Oct 15. The past year's highest closes were 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ, both on Oct 6. The data shows no news since the last note. No market gate is active.
note.business: Trend: both indices are labeled sideways. Each is above its 200-day average, so the long trend holds. Each is below its 50-day average, so the short trend is broken. QQQ is 4.4% below its 50-day and SPY is 1.0% below its own, so tech is further from repairing its short trend. Fear: the VIX reads 'normal' (the 15–20 band), at the 56th percentile of its past 252 readings. That reading is from Nov 11, because the Nov 12 value isn't stored yet. Breadth: 25% of stocks are above their 50-day averages. (General knowledge: breadth shows how many stocks take part in a move. A low reading means most stocks have not joined the bounce.) Together, the readings show no panic and an intact long-term trend. The recent rebound is narrow, though, and the short-term trend is not yet repaired. That mix tends to suit choosing individual names over buying broadly.

worth.text: This is a market-level note, and DATA contains no valuation inputs. The levels cited are trend references, not estimates of worth.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: Both SPY and QQQ remain above their 200-day averages (728.99 and 680.94), so the long-term trend counts as up.
Over 5 days, SPY is up 3.29% and QQQ is up 6.35%. Both are well above their Nov 5 lows of 733.00 and 647.05.
Fear is in the 'normal' band (56th percentile), not elevated or high.
bear: Both indices are below their 50-day averages (SPY 764.43, QQQ 718.46), so the short-term trend is broken. QQQ is 4.4% below its line.
Breadth is weak: only 25% of stocks are above their 50-day averages.
On a 20-day view, QQQ is down -5.47% and SPY -1.9%. Both remain below their 1-month highs, so the pullback is not recovered.

levels.what: SPY 50-day average: a close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 21): a close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.
QQQ 50-day average: a close above it would put the short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check. That would be the cue to lean in more.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 15): a close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 5): a close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline is continuing.
SPY 200-day average: a close below it would put the long-term trend down. That would be a stand-aside signal.
QQQ 200-day average (QQQ is 1.1% above it): a close below it would put tech's long-term trend down. That would be a stand-aside signal.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 5): a close below it would mean the tech decline is continuing.

longterm.why: The long-term trend holds and fear is normal, which argues against standing aside. The broken short-term trend and 25% breadth argue against leaning in broadly. Together they favor only the strongest names over broad buying.

swing.why: QQQ closed at 688.17, below its 50-day average of 718.46. Per the trend gates, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check until QQQ closes above that level.

decision.timing: PPI comes out Nov 13 at 08:30. It is an early read on inflation pressure. NVDA reports earnings on an estimated Nov 17, after the close. Per DATA, its big index weight means the report moves the whole tech group. Both events are close enough to push the indices toward or away from the gate levels. note.headline: Tesla touches the top of its own valuation history while cash flow shrinks

summary.thesis: Tesla's price assumes very fast growth, but sales were flat last quarter and margins and free cash flow are falling.
summary.decision: Long-term: avoid. Swing: wait, because the price sits just under resistance and the setup is poor.
summary.act_at: Reconsider below 293.94 or on a close above 417.44

note.happening: TSLA closed at 397.45, up 1.69% on the day. That is just under the top of its own-history valuation range (399.81) and below resistance at 408.62–417.44. The Verge reported that Cybertruck fans are turning on Elon Musk after he 'pulls the plug'; the headline does not say exactly what was stopped. The next earnings report is due on 2027-01-27.
note.business: Several numbers point to a weaker business. Sales growth in the latest quarter was -0.17% from a year earlier, compared with 15.78% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, fell from 4.74% to 3.35%. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after investment, fell from 6.8B to 3.3B. The filings also flag a demand warning: inventory is up 15% while latest-quarter sales are up 0%. Unsold cars can lead to price cuts and thinner margins. The balance sheet is not at risk. Tesla has 17.9B in cash, 8.0B in debt, 37.5B in net cash and 45.4B in total liquidity. Dilution (new shares diluting existing owners) is small at 0.43% a year. The Cybertruck report mainly affects sentiment and brand loyalty for now. Our data has no segment breakdown, so we cannot measure how much that product matters to revenue. A single product decision is a smaller issue than flat total sales and shrinking cash flow (general knowledge).

worth.text: The two valuation methods give very different answers. A discounted cash flow model values the company today based on the cash it should produce in future. Starting from 3.3B of trailing free cash flow, it gives 20.23 (bear), 25.02 (base) and 45.34 (bull) per share. Even with a 30% starting growth rate, the value is only 45.55. The filings estimate that the price needs about 51% a year growth, compared with 3% a year delivered over three years. The other method asks what Tesla is worth if investors keep paying the same price-to-sales multiple they have paid over the last five years. That gives 203.8 (low), 293.94 (mid) and 399.81 (high). Today's price-to-sales of 15.2 sits at the 77th percentile of its own 5-year history. The trailing P/E is 437.3. The whole gap comes down to one assumption: does the market keep valuing Tesla on sales and its story, or on the cash it actually produces? Even on the generous method, 397.45 is near the top.
worth.key_assumption: The market keeps valuing Tesla within its own 5-year price-to-sales range rather than on current free cash flow.

bull: The balance sheet is strong: net cash of 37.5B and liquidity of 45.4B give room to invest through a slow patch.
The valuation inputs include analysts' next-year EPS growth of 25%. If that happens, the growth gap narrows.
The price is above its 50-day average (374.46) and 200-day average (382.86), and is still inside its own-history valuation range that tops out at 399.81.
bear: The price needs about 51% a year growth, compared with 3% a year delivered over 3 years and 8.3% over the last 12 months.
Trailing free cash flow fell from 6.8B to 3.3B, and operating margin fell from 4.74% to 3.35%.
Inventory is up 15% while latest-quarter sales are up 0%, which raises the risk of price cuts.

levels.what: Today's close. This is near the top of the history-based range and far above every cash-flow value.
The top of the own-history price-to-sales range. Above it, even the generous method says the stock is expensive.
The middle of the own-history range. Here the price would no longer depend on Tesla holding a top-of-range multiple.

longterm.why: This is a grade D business. Sales are flat and margins and cash flow are falling, yet the stock trades near the top of its own valuation history. The rules committee call is also Avoid.

swing.why: The stock is moving sideways, with flat averages, in a zone from 393.63 to 400.51 just under resistance at 408.62–417.44. The room up to that ceiling is small next to the 16.57 average daily range. A close above 417.44, or a pullback into support at 380.15–389.95, would give a cleaner setup.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-01-27 land after the 2027-01-15 options expiry. Options price about a 5.5% move by 2026-11-20 and 14.1% by 2027-01-15, with implied volatility of 42.5 against realized volatility of 61.2. That makes the January report the main catalyst, not the coming weeks.

change_mind: The next report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and trailing free cash flow climbing back toward 6.8B.
Quarterly sales growth returns toward the 15.78% of two quarters ago, and inventory growth no longer outpaces sales.
Price drops to the 293.94 middle of the own-history range, or closes below support at 364.02–368.6. Either would reset both the valuation and the swing picture.
note.what_changed: Since yesterday's note the price rose from 390.84 to 397.45, almost touching the 399.81 top of the own-history range, and a Cybertruck fan backlash was reported. Neither changes the falling margins and cash flow, so the view stays at avoid and wait.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: NVIDIA: CEO exit and probe hit the stock; strong business waits on earnings

summary.thesis: The business is still growing fast and earning record margins, and the price assumes less growth than our base case, but the reported CEO exit and investigation make the near term unclear.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, and wait for the 2026-11-17 earnings report before adding. Swing: no trade into earnings.
summary.act_at: Hold at 166.19; add near 156.62 after earnings; reassess near 228.42

note.happening: NVDA fell 4.34% to 166.19. Many outlets reported that CEO Jensen Huang has left, and that an investigation is under way with outside lawyers; a report tying a family member to a Chinese competitor is marked speculative. Earnings are due on 2026-11-17, and option prices point to a 9.9% move around the report.
note.business: Nothing in today's news changes the latest reported numbers. Quarterly sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, faster than the 73.21% of two quarters before. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) reached 127.0B, up from 72.0B, and the company holds 23.2B more cash than debt. Analysts raised next-year EPS (earnings per share) 23.9% over 90 days, and it was flat over the last 30 days (-0.04%). The CEO exit is a governance and sentiment shock first. Whether it affects strategy, customer relationships or support for open-source software is an open question (general knowledge); TechCrunch reported that the open-source question has already come up. The real business risks come from the filings and were there before today. Margin sits at the top of its 5-year range (16–65%). Unpaid customer bills grew 127% while sales grew 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are stretched. Insiders also sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans. Demand and cash flow are not at risk on today's evidence. How long margins stay this high, and leadership continuity, are.

worth.text: At 166.19 the stock trades at 20.9 times trailing earnings and 10.4 times next year's expected earnings. Its price-to-sales ratio of 13.2 is below the peer median of 17.1 and in the 9th percentile of its own 5-year history. The discounted-cash-flow (DCF) model values future cash at 195.92 (bear), 228.42 (base) and 272.22 (bull). The stock's own price-to-sales history gives 217.35–411.04. Today's price implies free cash flow growing about 21.5% a year at the start. The gap between methods comes almost entirely from that starting growth rate: 30% gives 228.42, 20% gives 156.62 and 10% gives 105.89. Margin matters just as much. If operating margin fell to 48%, value would drop to 117.71, and at 32% to 78.79. The automated rule says 'Buy now', while the committee says 'Hold'. I use 156.62–228.42 as the fair-value range because margins at a 5-year peak and fast-rising receivables argue against the higher history-based values.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing 20–30% a year and operating margin stays near today's 65%, rather than falling toward 48%.

bull: Growth is speeding up, not slowing: quarterly sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters ago.
The price is low for the growth: 10.4 times next year's expected earnings, and price-to-sales of 13.2 against a peer median of 17.1.
Cash is strong: free cash flow of 127.0B (up from 72.0B) and net cash of 23.2B give room to handle a leadership transition.
bear: Margins may be at a peak: operating margin of 65% is the top of its 5-year range, and at 48% the model value falls to 117.71.
Unpaid customer bills rose 127% while sales rose 106%, a possible sign of pulled-forward demand or stretched customers.
The chart is weak: price 166.19 sits below the 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (201.25, 215.94, 204.07), and no support zone is listed below.

levels.what: Today's close. It is inside the fair-value range and implies only about 21.5% starting cash-flow growth. That is enough to hold, but not enough to add before earnings and with leadership unclear.
Value at 20% starting growth, the low end of the range. This is an area to add after earnings if margins and receivables hold up.
Base-case DCF value. Near here the valuation upside is used up, so reassess.

longterm.why: The business numbers support the stock, and the automated rule says buy. A confirmed leadership change, a reported investigation and earnings five days away argue for holding rather than adding now.

swing.why: The stock is in a downtrend with no listed support below. Resistance sits just above at 169.91–175.15 (5 touches). Earnings fall inside any swing window, and an implied move of 9.9% against an ATR (average daily range) of 9.85 means the report can gap past any stop.

decision.timing: Wait for the 2026-11-17 report. Implied volatility of 74.4 against 54.0 realized shows the market expects a big move. Act only after the report shows whether margins and receivables hold, and once there is clarity on leadership.

change_mind: The report misses the quarter's consensus of 2.47 EPS on 109.0B revenue, or the company guides operating margin well below 65.21%. That would push value toward 117.71 and shift the view to avoid or trim.
Receivables again grow faster than sales (127% vs 106% last time). That would point to weakening demand quality and argue against adding at 156.62.
A clean report plus a close back above the 169.91–175.15 resistance zone would reopen a swing entry and support adding toward the 228.42 base value.
note.what_changed: Since the 2026-11-11 note, the price fell from 173.73 to 166.19, the 162.81–164.98 support zone no longer appears, and further governance reports came out. The view stays at hold and no trade, because the business data and fair-value range are unchanged.

note.headline: AMD jumps 5.86% to 585.3; strong business, but price still far above value

summary.thesis: AMD is growing faster and earning better margins, but at 585.3 the price assumes years of very high growth that our valuation methods do not support.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: wait. The price sits in the middle of a busy trading zone, and no clean trend has formed.
summary.act_at: Long-term near 333.38; swing on a hold of 546.44–562.99 or a close above 596.07

note.happening: AMD closed at 585.3, up 5.86% on the day. There were no new news items since the last note. The price is now inside the 574.2–596.07 zone where it has traded often, above its 50-day average of 552.99 and well above its 200-day average of 421.71. The next earnings report is on 2027-02-02, so for now the main driver is the price itself, not new information.
note.business: The business itself is getting stronger. Quarterly sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier, faster than the 37.85% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of each sales dollar left after running costs, rose to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, rose to 7.1B from 5.4B. The balance sheet is sound, with net cash of 8.7B. Analysts raised next-year EPS estimates by 12.1% in 30 days. These numbers point to real demand, not just a better mood. Today's 5.86% jump, by contrast, changes sentiment only: no filing or news came with it. The filings do flag two real risks. Inventory is up 57% while quarterly sales are up 45%, and unsold chips can force price cuts. Also, the 18% operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range, and margins at a peak tend to fade. Cash and debt are not the risk here. The risk is the margin and the price.

worth.text: Every valuation method puts fair value far below the price. A discounted cash flow model, which values the company on the cash it may earn in the future, gives 148.51 (bear), 190.99 (base) and 226.75 (bull). Valuing AMD at the price-to-sales levels it usually trades at gives 179.24 to 333.38. The stock trades at 21.1 times sales, against a peer median of 14.7, and sits at its 93rd percentile of its own 5-year range. It costs 127.6 times trailing earnings and 33.1 times analysts' next-year EPS of 17.69. The gap between the price and the models comes from growth. The cash flow model caps starting growth at 30%. Analysts' next-year EPS forecast implies 119% growth. Even 30% growth gives only 190.99. Margins also matter: if operating margin falls to 13%, the value drops to 100.61. The price makes sense only if the forecast earnings surge happens and holds for years.
worth.key_assumption: The models allow at most 30% starting growth, fading over ten years, while the price needs something closer to analysts' 119% next-year EPS growth to last.

bull: Growth is speeding up: quarterly sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier, up from 37.85% two quarters ago.
Profitability nearly doubled: operating margin rose to 17.72% from 8.78%.
Analysts keep raising their numbers: next-year EPS of 17.69 is up 12.1% in 30 days, which brings the forward multiple down to 33.1.
bear: The price is above every method: fair value tops out at 333.38, and the base cash flow value is 190.99.
Inventory is up 57% while quarterly sales are up 45%. Unsold product can force price cuts.
Margins at a peak are fragile: at a 13% operating margin, the value falls to 100.61.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a price to buy at.
Bottom of the 546.44–562.99 support zone, tested 5 times. It is a better entry point if earnings keep beating, though still above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range (high end of its own price-to-sales history). This is where the valuation case begins.

longterm.why: The business is improving quickly, but the price already assumes the best case. The highest fair value of 333.38 sits far below 585.3.

swing.why: The trend is a range, and the price sits inside the 574.2–596.07 zone after a 5.86% day. A typical daily move (ATR) is 40.14. A setup would be a pullback that holds 546.44–562.99, or a close above 596.07 with room up to the 639.0–658.52 resistance zone.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-02-02 are not close yet. Options price in a 15.6% move by 2026-12-18 and a 19.7% move by 2027-01-15, so large swings are expected even before the report.

change_mind: The case gets stronger if the next report beats the 2.93 EPS and 17.1B revenue consensus and inventory growth falls back below sales growth (now 57% vs 45%).
Operating margin falling back toward 13% would point to the 100.61 value scenario and confirm the bear case.
A close above the 639.0–658.52 resistance zone would make the swing view more constructive. A break below 517.35 would mean the range is failing.
note.what_changed: The price rose from 552.9 to 585.3, and the support zones are now mapped higher (546.44–562.99 and 517.35–530.13). The view has not changed, because the business data is the same and the price is now even further above the 148.51–333.38 value range.

note.headline: Amazon edges just above its value range while cash burn keeps the case on hold

summary.thesis: Amazon's margins are improving, but the business burns cash, growth is slowing, and the stock trades above the top of its own-history value range.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: wait, because the price sits in the middle of its trading range with no clear edge.
summary.act_at: Look again near 251.93–257.04; fair value meets price at 238.65

note.happening: Amazon closed at 267.44, up 0.48% on the day. That is just above the top of its value range of 187.93–266.17. The only relevant news is a reported Microsoft outage in which AWS and Google users also reported issues (CNBC). No earnings date is in the data, and the latest quarterly filing came on 2026-10-30.
note.business: Some things are changing the business itself. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 13.09% from 11.02%. That is real progress. Cash is going the other way. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and investing in it) was -46.9B over the last 12 months, down from 10.6B a year earlier, a margin of -5.88%. Net debt (debt minus cash) is 66.7B, against total debt of 180.9B and cash of 55.8B. Growth is slowing. Sales rose 12.09% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, down from 16.61% two quarters ago. Filings also show unpaid customer bills up 61% while sales rose 12%. That can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. Heavy investment spending is the likely cause of the cash burn (general knowledge), but our data has no segment detail to confirm it. Other things move only sentiment. The reported AWS outage is a headline. Nothing in the data shows lost demand from it. Liquidity, the cash and credit Amazon can draw on, is 114.2B, so its ability to fund itself is not at risk. What is at risk is the market's patience with spending that does not yet return cash.

worth.text: No discounted-cash-flow value is possible here, because free cash flow is negative. That leaves one method: Amazon's own price-to-sales history. Price-to-sales compares the company's market value with its yearly revenue. Amazon's ratio sat at its 20th, 50th and 80th percentile of the past five years at 187.93, 238.65 and 266.17 per share. Today's 3.6 times sales is at the 80th percentile, and the price of 267.44 is just above the top of that range. Against peers the stock looks cheap. The peer median is 6.7 times sales, and the growth-adjusted ratio is 0.61 of peers. The gap between the two views comes down to one question: should Amazon be valued against its own past or against faster-valued peers like MSFT and GOOGL? On earnings, the stock trades at 21.7 times trailing profit and 20.9 times this year's estimate. On next year's estimate it is 25.1 times, because analysts expect earnings per share to fall to 10.67 from 12.8. Filings also note that the price implies about 34% a year growth, while Amazon delivered 13% a year over 3 years.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range rather than moving toward the peer median of 6.7.

bull: Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales is turning into more profit.
At 3.6 times sales against a peer median of 6.7, and 0.61 of peers after adjusting for growth, the stock is cheap next to its large-tech peers.
Analysts raised next year's earnings estimate by 1.4% over the last 30 days, and liquidity of 114.2B covers the spending.
bear: Free cash flow fell to -46.9B from 10.6B a year earlier, and net debt now stands at 66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, while unpaid customer bills rose 61%.
The price of 267.44 sits above the top of its own value range at 266.17, and the business quality grade is D (score 53.4).

levels.what: Top of the own-history value range. The price is just above it, so this is not a place to start buying.
Bottom of the strongest support zone (251.93–257.04, 6 touches), where buyers have stepped in before. A better entry if cash flow stops getting worse.
Midpoint of the own-history value range, where price and fair value meet.

longterm.why: Margins are improving, but cash burn and slowing growth do not justify a price above the top of the value range. The rule-based verdict is 'Too expensive', and the committee call is 'Avoid'.

swing.why: The trend is a sideways range, and the 20-, 50- and 200-day averages are all flat. The price sits between support at 258.08–261.12 and resistance at 274.75–278.56, too close to both for a stop and a target to give good balance. Recent swings (realized volatility 42.4) have also been bigger than options price in (implied volatility 33.4).

decision.timing: No earnings date is in the data, and options to 2026-11-20 price a move of about 4.3%, so a test of 258.08–261.12 support or 274.75–278.56 resistance is the next point to reassess.

change_mind: Free cash flow margin climbs from -5.88% back toward positive, which would open up a cash-flow valuation and support the peer-style view.
The price falls into the 251.93–257.04 support zone while operating margin holds at 13.09% or better, putting it back inside the value range.

Quarterly sales growth climbs back from 12.09% toward 16.61% and unpaid bills (up 61%) grow closer to sales, or the price closes above the 274.75–278.56 resistance with options open interest at 290 coming into play.
note.what_changed: The price moved from 266.17 to 267.44 and the trend now reads as a sideways range rather than down, but no new filings or business news arrived, so the view stays at wait.

note.headline: Microsoft holds steady: growth and margins improve, but cash flow still lags the price

summary.thesis: Microsoft's sales and profit margins keep improving, but heavy spending has cut free cash flow, so the price only makes sense if that spending pays off.
summary.decision: Hold for the long term; wait on a swing trade until the price reaches a clearer level.

note.happening: Microsoft closed at 523.0, up 0.36%, in the middle of a sideways range. Cerebras reported a deal with Microsoft, and Outlook was reported down in an outage that also touched AWS and Google users. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
note.business: The core business keeps getting better. Sales grew 18.8% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, up from 18.3% two quarters ago. The operating margin, meaning the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. Cash is the weak spot. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after investment, fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and the filings note that each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year against 51¢ three years ago. The reported Cerebras deal fits that spending story: it looks like more AI computing capacity, which adds to costs before it adds to sales. The Outlook outage mainly hurts sentiment and reputation for now. Short outages rarely change demand for core software (general knowledge), unless they keep happening. The balance sheet is safe, with 29.0B in net cash. What's at risk is the payback on the spending, not demand or solvency.

worth.text: The answer depends on whether you value today's cash flow or today's earnings. A cash-flow model (DCF) that starts from the 60.0B of trailing free cash flow gives 184.7 to 296.75 per share, with a base case of 223.82. To justify the current price, that model needs free cash flow to start growing about 41.0% a year, while sales have grown 17–18% and analysts expect earnings to grow 21%. Even 30% growth only gets to 352.37. Against its own history, the stock looks fair. Its price-to-sales ratio is at the 40th percentile of the last five years, which gives a range of 475.73 to 592.92 with a midpoint of 535.43. Earnings multiples are 27.3 times trailing earnings and 21.6 times next year's. Against peers it looks expensive: 11.2 times sales versus a peer median of 4.1. The whole gap between the methods comes from the depressed cash flow. If the spending turns back into cash, the history-based range is the right guide. If it doesn't, the stock is well above fair value.
